text:
The Devils traded for Connor Hellebuyck on Oct. 23, and he has been their biggest story since. Some of it is hockey, including a start where he was pulled after a disastrous first period. Some of it is much heavier: Hellebuyck has said the threats against his family went beyond online death threats. That is a hard thing to carry into a new dressing room, and it deserves to be said plainly before any save percentage.

The team in front of him is very good. New Jersey is 17-8-0 with 34 points and gets 57% of the expected goals (the quality of chances for and against), 56% at 5v5. The Devils take only 2.76 penalties a game, and their kill allows only 0.48 expected goals a game. Brett Pesce and Luke Hughes have been on for 23 goals for and 12 against.

The worry is the net, which is surprising given who they traded for. The Devils have allowed about 8.3 more goals than their chances deserved, and Jake Allen is at .858 over his last five starts. If the goaltending turns average, this record gets better, not worse.

Injuries bite: Anthony Mantha is out at least a month after throat surgery and Johnathan Kovacevic four to six weeks with a high-ankle sprain. Jack Hughes, meanwhile, has the hockey world arguing about his all-white skates. Our simulations give the Devils a 96% playoff chance. What to watch: Hellebuyck's next five starts.
headline: Hellebuyck is here, and so are the questions
